questions.q: What is an Agent operator, structurally?
options: A job step subsystem
A notification destination — a person or distribution list — with no logic of its own
A schedule attached to a job
A condition that watches for a specific error
questions.explain: An operator (sp_add_operator) is purely a destination, typically an email address; it doesn't watch for anything itself.

questions.q: What two things can an alert do when its condition fires?
options: Notify an operator, run a job, or both
Automatically restart the SQL Server service
Automatically create a new linked server
Only send an email — nothing else
questions.explain: An alert reacts to its watched condition by notifying an operator, running a job, or both — the two are independent response options.

questions.q: Which stored procedure creates the link between an existing alert and an existing operator?
options: sp_add_operator
sp_add_notification
sp_attach_schedule
sp_add_alert
questions.explain: sp_add_alert creates the alert and sp_add_operator creates the operator, but sp_add_notification is the separate call that links them and sets the notification method.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what severity level is a realistic threshold for paging an on-call DBA?
options: Only severity 25, catastrophic failures
Severity 16 or higher
Severity 1, informational messages only
Severity has no relationship to alert configuration
questions.explain: Severity 16 and above generally indicates errors serious enough to need human attention, making it a common real-world alert threshold.

questions.q: Why might a DBA create an alert on a specific error number, like 9002, instead of relying only on a severity-based alert?
options: Severity-based alerts are deprecated in favor of error-number alerts
Specific error numbers cannot trigger severity-based alerts at all
A specific error number lets the alert carry a more targeted, actionable message than a generic severity catch-all
Error 9002 has no defined severity level
questions.explain: Error 9002 (transaction log full) is severity 17 but specific enough that a dedicated alert with a targeted message is more useful than a broad severity-17 alert.
